questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Berkeley being at the front of my favorite research field (labor economics). Further I choosde the US because of how easy it is to find courses in english.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I went to an introduction meeting and orientation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I do find it a bit expensive since it cost 200 dollars to attend orientation.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found a room in an shared apartment through Airbnb which was quite easy. However, berkeley in generel is very expensive and it is hard to find something affordable.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is certainly cheaper, however you have to make an ekstra effort to meet other student, compared to living in a dorm.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: As an undeclared major student, you are second in line for a lot of courses, however it is possible to get enrolled in most classes from the waiting list.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was quite a lot of information about the courses available on their website.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was waitlisted for 3 of 4 courses, but was enrolled in all of them in the end. Hence, very successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do not be concerned if you get waitlisted for a course, most people end up getting the course anyway. Further, berkeley say you should only expect to enroll in 1-2 courses from you major, i got into 3 economic classes (+ 1 from another major), which was very fitting.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the upper-division economics courses at Berkeley are at a level somewhat similar to the elective courses at KU (maybe slightly lower). However, there is a lot less math.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There is a lot more participation during the lectures at Berkeley. Further, I do believe the workload in terms of assignments is a bit higher at Berkeley. Lastly, they place greater emphasis on economic intuition and empirical papers, and less on mathematical derivations.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ECON 151 Labor economics
ECON 131 Public ecnomics
ECON 191 Topics in economic research
STAT 33B Introduction to advanced programming in R

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend both Labor economics and Public economics, as Berkeley has some of the most renowned researchers from these areas. Furthermore, I really enjoyed the opportunity to write a seminar paper in Topics in Economic Research, which is very nice as a master student.

questions.answer: I did not really encounter any unexpected cost.

questions.answer: Food was a lot more expensive compared to what I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Berkeley has  A LOT of clubs.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Any kind og club you can imagine, Berkeley has.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Just attend anything which sound interesting, whether its is a hike or a debate. Berkeley has a lot of very nice hiking trails on 1-2 km from campus.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: If you have time after your exchange, I would highly recommend renting a car and visiting different national parks. I personally visited Yosemite, Death Valley, Zion, and the Grand Canyon, all of which had great hikes. Yosemite and the Grand Canyon were my favorites.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: In general, Americans are very open.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I personally mostly spent time with other exchange students, I think getting more engaged in the clubs would have helped getting to know more local students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did have to get used to all the small talk at the grocery stores and on public transportation.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are very open and very nice.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) It is very normal to get waitlisted for a course and get enrolled later
2) The grocery stores are often very expensive, i personally found Trader Joe's to be the most reasonable
3) There is a lot of homelessness in both San Francisco and Berkeley.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I know another student who, instead of getting UC's own health insurance, got another cheaper one.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To experience another culture

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Navigating the application process

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
